DR_LEGENDS.name: Stu Hungar
DR_LEGENDS.style: Reads you before you read your cards. Three-time world champ, a legend for a reason.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Kid, I've seen this hand before. You haven't.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Colt the Cowboy
DR_LEGENDS.style: The godfather. Aggressive before aggressive was cool. Loves ten-deuce.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Son, I was playing this game before your daddy could shuffle.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Chance Cage
DR_LEGENDS.style: Slow-plays monsters and lets you hang yourself.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Take your time. I always do.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Armadillo Fatts
DR_LEGENDS.style: Spins yarns between hands and steals your blinds during the punchline.
DR_LEGENDS.line: I've got more stories than you've got chips, partner.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Chris Schillings
DR_LEGENDS.style: Won it all off an $86 satellite. Proof the dream is real.
DR_LEGENDS.line: I was you once. Spreadsheets and all. Play your game.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Phil Hellraiser
DR_LEGENDS.style: Most bracelets ever, and he will tell you. Tight, then explodes when he loses.
DR_LEGENDS.line: If there were no luck in poker, I would win every single one of these.

DR_LEGENDS.name: GG Negroni
DR_LEGENDS.style: Talks through every hand and usually says your cards out loud.
DR_LEGENDS.line: I put you on ace-queen. Am I close? I'm close.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Gus Handsome
DR_LEGENDS.style: Plays any two cards, and makes it work just often enough.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Seven-four suited. My favourite hand. Today.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Antonio Escandalo
DR_LEGENDS.style: Smooth, fearless, and the chips just seem to disappear.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Watch closely. Now your stack is gone.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Mouthy Michael
DR_LEGENDS.style: Never stops talking. Never stops jamming.
DR_LEGENDS.line: You call this? You're not calling this. You're NOT calling this.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Sammy Smokes
DR_LEGENDS.style: Pure feel. Bets like he owns the casino.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Is a nice hand. Is not my hand, but is nice.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Erik Sidle
DR_LEGENDS.style: Thirty years at the top without saying thirty words.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Tom "hrrrm" Swan
DR_LEGENDS.style: Six-figure bluffs with nothing, on purpose.
DR_LEGENDS.line: I have air. Do you want to find out?

DR_LEGENDS.name: Patrik Antionius
DR_LEGENDS.style: Never blinks. Never tilts. Never stops.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Your move.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Fedor Holdz
DR_LEGENDS.style: Retired at the top, came back, kept winning.
DR_LEGENDS.line: I studied this exact spot this morning.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Justin Bonanza
DR_LEGENDS.style: Biggest single-year score in history. Calm, mathematical, relentless.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Equilibrium says call. So I call.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Bryn Kenny-Kash
DR_LEGENDS.style: Plays the biggest games on the planet like they are $1/$2.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Nice stack. I will take it.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Stephen Chillwick
DR_LEGENDS.style: Final table every week. Never flustered.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Good luck. Genuinely.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Jason Kahoon
DR_LEGENDS.style: Works out at 5 AM, studies at 6, wins Titans by dinner.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Discipline beats talent. I have both.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Linus Loophole
DR_LEGENDS.style: Plays so close to perfect that the solver checks HIS work.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Your frequency is off by four percent.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Isaac Hackston
DR_LEGENDS.style: Four cards or two, he has solved it.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Interesting sizing. Incorrect, but interesting.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Michael Addemup
DR_LEGENDS.style: Wins the biggest buy-ins in the world, then disappears.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Shove.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Alex Foxglove
DR_LEGENDS.style: Top of the leaderboard so often they named the trophy room after him.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Leaderboard points are points.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Kristen Foxglove
DR_LEGENDS.style: Multiple player-of-the-year titles. Reads people for a living.
DR_LEGENDS.line: You're nervous. Your left hand gives it away.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Artur Martini
DR_LEGENDS.style: Shaken, never stirred. Top of the Titan rankings.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Another one for the cabinet.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Jesse Lonestar
DR_LEGENDS.style: Nine wins in one year. When he goes gorilla mode, run.
DR_LEGENDS.line: GORILLA. MODE.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Kayhan Mocha
DR_LEGENDS.style: Topped the money list with a $7.7 million invitational win.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Cold out there. Colder in here.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Seth Daisies
DR_LEGENDS.style: First bracelet was a $250K Super High Roller. Started at the top.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Go big or go home. I went big.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Bernhard Bindr
DR_LEGENDS.style: Came out of nowhere with a $10 million win. Like you.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Everyone was a nobody once.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Punnat Punchline
DR_LEGENDS.style: Three Titan titles in one year. All business.
DR_LEGENDS.line: This is my office.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Nicky Parmesan
DR_LEGENDS.style: Three bracelets in one summer. Mixed-game wizard.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Pick a game. Any game.

DR_LEGENDS.name: Michael Mizrockie
DR_LEGENDS.style: Won the Main Event and the Players Championship in the same summer. Defending champ.
DR_LEGENDS.line: Defending champ. You'll have to take it from me.

satbubble: Satellite bubble: once you have a seat locked up, folding aces can be right. Survival is the only prize.
Short stacks have to gamble. Big stacks don't. Know which one you are.
middle: The short stacks are getting desperate. Let them shove into your good hands.
Stack sizes changed. Your opening ranges should too.
This is where tournaments are won quietly. Steal, don't spew.
deep: You're in the money. Ladder up, but don't play scared. Scared money never wins.
Every pay jump matters now. Pick on the stacks that are clinging on.
early: Early levels: chips are cheap, mistakes aren't. Fold the junk and let them spew.
Position is power. The button prints money; under the gun is a tax.
You don't have to win a hand to win this level. Survive and steal.
bubble: Bubble. The short stacks are terrified. The big stacks are licking their lips. Which one are you?
Near the money, a call costs more than chips. Tighten your calls, not your raises.
Min-cash is not the goal. But busting on the bubble is a long ride home.
final: Final table. Every pay jump is real money. Every chip is a decision.
Short stack? Your jam is your weapon. Raise-fold gives it away.
Look around. Somebody here is scared. Make sure it isn't you.
cash: Cash game: no bubble, no pay jumps. Just chip EV. Play the math.
Steal the blinds you can. Defend the ones you should.

brilliant.line: The hard, brave play, and the right one.

great.line: A close spot most players miss. You found it.

excellent.line: Basically as good as the best play.

good.line: A play the solver makes too.

inaccuracy.line: Not a disaster, but it leaks value.

mistake.line: This costs real money over time.

blunder.line: A big leak. Study this one.

beats.t:
Monday. 6:47 PM. Floor 34.
Everyone else went home an hour ago.
The Henderson deck. Redo it. All of it. On my desk by eight.
I sent it Friday. You signed off on it.
And now I'm un-signing off on it. Problem?
No problem, Lou.
Great. Oh, and I told the partners the new model was my idea. Team player, right?

You were nine the first time you saw it on TV.
A final table under hot lights. A man in dark glasses pushed every chip he had into the middle with nothing.

The room went silent. His opponent folded. He never showed.
He made it look like he could see the future.
Somewhere along the way I traded that for a lanyard.

2:13 AM. The deck is done.
You are not.
You're doing the thing where you stare at the pie like it owes you money.
Long day.
Long life, by the look of it. What do you do?
Spreadsheets. For a guy who takes credit for them.
And what did you want to do?

line.t: Ha. Everybody says that at 2 AM. Almost nobody means it.
It always matters. You just stopped saying it out loud.

beats.t: He slides a red envelope across the counter.
Riverside Local Championship. Saturday, noon. Two-fifty seat. It's paid.
Why would you give that to a stranger?
Because I sat on that stool once. Somebody bought my pie too.
Three things. Fold the junk. Pressure the scared ones. And near the money, think about what the money's worth, not the chips.
Who are you?
People call me Slick.

He drops cash for both checks and is gone before the bell over the door stops ringing.
Inside the envelope: a seat card, and one line in pen.
“People insist on calling it luck…”
You look different. Did you finish the Henderson numbers?
__fn
Hello? I'm talking to you. Weekend's over, champ.
Decision time.
Lou? Redo it yourself.

The elevator ride down is the best thirty-four floors of your life.
You have $1,200 in savings and absolutely no plan B.
Heard about Saturday. Riverside runs games every night. Start small. Never play above your roll. Text me when you win something.
BRO. YOU QUIT YOUR JOB?? CALL ME

You keep the lanyard.
But tonight you open a new spreadsheet and name it BANKROLL.
$2,000 in savings. Days for Corporate Lou. Nights for the dream.
Heard about Saturday. Riverside runs games every night. Start small. Never play above your roll. Text me when you win something.

Riverside Card Room. Carpet from 1994. Coffee from this morning, maybe.
Twenty tables, every one of them a classroom.
New face. Sign the list. One-two has a seat in ten. Nightly turbo kicks off at seven.
Hey, you're the kid from Saturday. Don't get cocky. This room eats dreamers for breakfast.
Cute hoodie. Did it come with the free seat?

Mustich. Dad's money, a solver subscription, and a smile you want to wipe off.
He's been circling the Riverside Classic all year.
Goal: win the Riverside Classic, or build your bankroll to $10,000.
You've outgrown Riverside. The Circuit stops at Silver Strike this month. Every event gives a ring. Go get one.
Bigger rooms. Better players. A guy at the rail is wearing four rings on one hand.
You're the kid who quit the cubicle? I was an accountant. Spreadsheets and everything. Play your game and let them find out.
Look who followed me to the Circuit. Try not to bust on the bubble this time.
Goal: win two Circuit rings and build a $40,000 bankroll.
Las Vegas in June. 112 degrees outside, 68 inside, and ten thousand people chasing the same gold.
Every kid who ever loved this game dreams about a bracelet. This is the room where they hand them out.

At the feature table sits a man in dark glasses. Fourteen bracelets. Nobody has seen him smile.
The man from TV. The reason you're here.
Kid. Stop looking at me and look at your cards.
Another internet kid. I'll see you at the final table. Probably not, though.
Goal: win a gold bracelet.
Welcome back to the feature table! Joining us: the cubicle kid with a bracelet, and people are calling it a fluke.
People insist on calling it luck.
Ooh. We have a quote. Producers, put that on a T-shirt.
Cameras make people do stupid things. Don't be people.
Goal: win two Tour titles (Royal Tour or GLO Cup) and build a $750,000 bankroll.
A private terminal. A plane with your name on the manifest. A buy-in that used to be a house.
Funny. Dad stopped staking me last month. Guess we're both self-made now.
I reviewed your last final table. Your bubble frequencies are… acceptable.
In here nobody's scared. Everyone knows the math. So the edge is in the spots they don't study. Find them.
Goal: win two Titan titles and build a $5,000,000 bankroll.

Eight thousand four hundred and two players. Ten thousand dollars each.
One of them will be on the cover of every poker magazine in the world.
Defending champ. If you want it, you'll have to take it from me.
BRO YOU ARE ON TV?? SIT UP STRAIGHT
Nine-year-old you watched this on a fuzzy TV. Go show him how it ends.
Goal: win the Main Event.
Your picture hangs in the Hall of Legends now. Next to men you used to watch on a fuzzy TV.
Fourteen bracelets. That's the number. Come take it.
Goal: beat every legend and pass Bio The Ghost's fourteen bracelets.
Lucky Seven Diner. 2:13 AM. Same stool. Same pie. Empty wallet.
Busted?
Every last dollar.
Good. Now you're a poker player. Everybody goes broke once. The good ones learn why.
__fn
Saw the photo. Trophy, big grin, terrible lighting. Proud of you, kid.
Left something in your locker. Every champion needs a pair.

Inside: a pair of pixelated sunglasses and a note.
“Deal with it.”

Confetti. Cameras. A bracelet the size of a doorknob.
Somewhere, a nine-year-old with a fuzzy TV is losing his mind.
Good game, kid.
He takes off his glasses. For the first time anyone can remember, Bio The Ghost smiles.
Now you'll find out the hard part. Everyone will be hunting you.
Hey buddy! Long time! Saw you on TV. Listen, about that promotion…
You leave him on read.
People insist on calling it luck.
Let them.
Lucky Seven Diner. Same stool, same pie. The feeling is not the same.
I did everything right. Every decision. And I'm out.
Then you had a good day. You just did not get paid for it.
Over one hand, the cards pay whoever they like. Over ten thousand, they pay whoever studied. Play for the ten thousand.
Heard you got coolered. Brutal. Maybe this game just isn’t for everyone.
He's right about one thing. It isn't for everyone.
Good. Make sure it is for you. I keep count of the beats, by the way. The ones who make it all have a long list.
The last card hits the felt. The Riverside Classic is yours.
Enjoy it. Dad says the Classic is a rounding error.
Don't listen to him, kid. Thirty years I've been chasing that trophy. You earned it.
Your name goes on the board by the cage. Permanent marker. Congratulations.
A tournament director slides a heavy ring across the table. It barely fits. You put it on anyway.
First ring? I still remember mine. Don't put it in a drawer. Wear it every day you play.
One ring. Now go get another one.

They fasten the bracelet around your wrist and the room starts clapping before you realize it is for you.
Gold. Real gold. Your name in the record book forever.
Lucky. If I had been at that final table, we'd be talking about my bracelet number eighteen.
IS THAT REAL GOLD?? THE WHOLE GROUP CHAT SAW IT
Nine-year-old you is screaming right now. Let him.
Champion! Fifty thousand people are watching on stream. How does it feel?

line.t: THERE it is. The chat is going absolutely crazy.

choice.t: "I just tried to make good decisions."

line.t: Humble AND dangerous. The worst combination for everyone else.

beats.t: Nice result. Now everyone has a file on you. Welcome to the Tour.
A trident-shaped trophy, a wire transfer with too many zeros, and a room full of the best players alive nodding at you.
Congrats. Honestly. Turns out you can't buy what you've got.
Took you long enough to figure that out.
Ha. Rematch at the Main?
Hey buddy!! Long time. Saw your name on a poker site. Crazy! We're hiring a Senior Associate. Coffee?

line.t: You put the phone face down and go back to studying bubble spots.
Three dots appear. Then disappear. Then nothing, forever.

DR_COOLERS: Kings into aces. All the chips go in, and you never had a chance.
You flop a set. He flops the higher set. That is the whole story.
Ace-king versus queens, a coin flip for your tournament. The coin lands on its edge, then on queens.
Your all-in is called by the one hand in his range that beats you.
Runner-runner. You did nothing wrong. The deck did.
DR_COOLER_LINES: You played it right. That's all you control. People insist on calling it luck.
Write it down and let it go. The next hand does not know about this one.
Every legend has a list of these longer than their list of titles.
Bad beats are the tax on getting your money in good. Pay it and keep playing.
That one stings. Good. It means you care. Now go show the deck it was wrong.
